newsitem.title: THAILAND: Finance One wants Thai bank licence.
newsitem.headline: Finance One wants Thai bank licence.

text.p: Thailand's cash-strapped Finance One Plc said on Wednesday it wanted to apply for a bank licence as part of a plan to restructure operations and regain a foothold in the finance business.

The former top Thai finance company, whose planned merger with medium-sized Thai Danu Bank Plc collapsed last week, also said that a central bank-inspired plan to boost its capital by 8.28 billion baht ($318 million) would be adequate to ensure its financial stability.

"Under the present economic downturn of Thailand, the management believes that the proposed restructuring programme and redefining of the Finance One group's business strategy will not only bring financial stability to Finance One's operations, but also is the best solution to regain confidence...," it said in a statement.

The statement was made at a meeting between senior Finance One officials led by chief executive Pin Chakkapak and private market analysts to clarify the company's position ahead of a resumption in its share trading on Friday.

Finance One's shares were suspended when it began the merger process with Thai Danu Bank. But brokers expect a major sell-off of the company's shares when it resumes trading on May 30 because of negative publicity affecting the company.

The company also said that the book value of its shares were 12.14 baht per share. Some analysts believe that the company shares had dropped to around three or four baht in the unofficial grey market from 23.75 baht when trade was halted on February 28.
Finance One added that it was also looking for a partner to join its finance and securities unit Thana One.
